topics.topic: How should judge_execution obtain the failure-detail byte ceiling while remaining argument-driven?
questions: Must judge_execution use RELEASE_CEILING_FAILURE_DETAIL_BYTES_MAX when constructing failure_detail, or must all of its decisions depend only on observation, output_ports and bounds?
Must judge_execution use RELEASE_CEILING_FAILURE_DETAIL_BYTES_MAX, or must that ceiling be supplied through observation or bounds so it decides from only its arguments?

quotes: judge_execution: [BEHAVIOR] MUST decide from the observation, the output ports and the bounds it is given, nothing else, and run nothing.

judge_execution: [PROVENANCE] failure_detail MUST hold only the report's failure, the type and message of an exception that escaped module loading or run, cut to at most the imported RELEASE_CEILING_FAILURE_DETAIL_BYTES_MAX constant bytes at a UTF-8 character boundary; it holds nothing the code printed; it is None for succeeded and when no exception escaped.
judgement.why: The first passage forbids judge_execution from consulting anything beyond its arguments, while the second requires it to consult an imported constant.

topics.topic: How should the scratch-bound requirement be supplied or removed?
questions: Must a scratch bound be added to ResourceBounds or supplied by an imported constant, or must the scratch-bound outcome condition be removed?

quotes: judge_execution: [DETERMINISM_OR_ORDERING] When cleanup was confirmed the outcome is the first that holds, in this order of = models.SandboxOutcome: timeout when the deadline passed; resource_exhausted when the memory, process, scratch or output bound was hit, the channel bound included; sandbox_violation when the report holds any trap hit, even if the code caught it and returned a conforming dict; crashed when the report says crashed, the runner exited abnormally, or no returned message was read — the report's returned is None: read_runner_report always gives a RunnerReport, for a channel that carried nothing one with no trap hit, no resource hit, crashed false, failure None and returned None, so the observation always holds a report; contract_violation when the returned value is not a dict with exactly the output ports, an output is not_representable, its JSON text does not give canonical JSON through canonical_bytes, or fit_port_value with bounds.output_bytes as size bound does not fit an output to its port; otherwise succeeded. The stored value and spool ceilings are applied by the module that stores or spools an output.
ResourceBounds fields (exact, no others exist): wall_time_ms: int, memory_bytes: int, output_bytes: int, process_count: int
judgement.why: The ordering note requires a scratch bound, but the exact ResourceBounds surface contains no scratch bound and the prompt supplies no imported scratch-bound constant.

topics.topic: Whether plan_run records are limited to unexecuted nodes or may represent executed mapped elements
questions: Must these records be restricted to nodes for which no element executed, or may they represent an already-run element with a map_index?

quotes: a skipped_by_guard or upstream_failed record, which runs writes only for a node none of whose elements executed, concludes the whole node so at once, mapped or not

Such drafts are derived only from records already written and carry exactly: the run's run_id, the node's node_id, status skipped_by_guard or upstream_failed, no executed, no map_index unless an element of the node already ran, no inputs, no outputs, failure_detail, detail_code and resources_used None, and started_at and ended_at both the given now;
judgement.why: One passage restricts these records to nodes with no executed elements, while the other permits such a draft to carry a map_index when an element already ran.

topics.topic: Whether pinned contract ports may be read again during advance_run
questions: Must the node ports be read only once during advance_run, or is the additional read through read_implementation an intended exception?
Must the pinned contract version and its ports be read only once during advance_run, or may execute_function_element read them again?

quotes: they are read once per advance and passed to plan_run as one NodePorts per flow node in node_id order;
execute_function_element reads the same pinned contract version again through read_implementation, which gives the same ports, since a pinned version never changes.
judgement.why: One passage limits the port read to once per advance, while the other requires another read during that advance.

topics.topic: Recovery behavior for owner_approval waiting state without approval_id
questions: When the stored reason is owner_approval and the current ElementWaiting has the same reason but no approval_id, must it stand or be reached again?

quotes: ElementWaiting with reason owner_approval and no approval_id — an attempt resolved not_applied whose fresh approval was never requested — is reached again with reach_operation_element with the inputs its latest NodeExecution names;
judgement.why: The specific owner_approval-without-approval_id rule requires reaching the element again.
